purpose: Proposed review coverage for the sixteen replacement stages in this packet. This file contains no matching results, approval, baseline or release authority.
inputProvenance: Every input is synthetic editorial text adapted from this packet's research suggestions or written for this review. No private reader disclosure or production session data was used.
limitations: The positive cases propose a figure and stage for editorial evaluation; they are not assertions of an observed or guaranteed hard match.
These close-fit examples are intentionally diagnostic and do not constitute balanced, adversarial or representative matching coverage.

Negative probes identify only premises that must not be invented or used as the named replacement's rationale. They do not require rejection of the prompt, exclusion of every named figure, a fixed ranking, or a particular alternative match.
No matcher, model provider, reranker, embedding service, database or live application was exercised to produce this file.
Do not replace, relabel or report a pass against the immutable approved gold set using these proposed cases.
Exact reader ages below are synthetic fixture inputs, not newly established historical ages. Qualified historical envelopes remain qualified.

The application intake minimum is eighteen. Rudolph's age-eighteen positive proposal is explicitly a partial connection two years beyond the proposed historical envelope, not an age-identical episode or a measured success.
All targets refer to proposed rows in this packet, not proof that those stages are installed, selectable, approved or published.

positiveCases.input: I made my first song with someone else after hearing a rival's success, but our published work barely earned anything.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: First creative collaboration with a small commercial return; not abandonment or restored self-worth.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Within the proposed 18–19 publication-year envelope; the exact composition month is not established.

positiveCases.input: I got into college, but working to pay my way still does not cover food. I find it hard to tell people I need help.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Student subsistence work, insufficient resources and reluctance to disclose need; community support is part of the story, not promised to the reader.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Within the corrected approximate 24–27 envelope; birth-date uncertainty remains.

positiveCases.input: I am separated and need to keep writing for money while caring for my child. I finished the book but still dislike it.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Continuing difficult work during separation, with a completed result that does not resolve dissatisfaction.

positiveCases.input: I am already a musician, but I cannot learn some passages on my own. I want help from another player without pretending I know it all.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Practical learning through questions, rehearsal and support from other musicians; no addiction-recovery inference.

positiveCases.input: I completed the paperwork for my project, but a name mismatch means another signed form before the deadline.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: An administrative correction under a deadline, not rejection of the invention or an invented humiliation.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Matches the proposed age 27 for the documented paperwork period.

positiveCases.input: I want to contribute something useful, but the larger project is unfinished and I can only offer one part.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Offering an assembled contribution while stating that the larger undertaking is incomplete.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Matches the proposed age 56 at the dedication.

positiveCases.input: People praise my work because of my background, but I want useful criticism that helps me learn.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Asking for meaningful criticism rather than condescending praise; no assumption that the requested visit occurred.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Within the qualified approximate 19–20 range; an exact birthday is not established.

positiveCases.input: My young child has come to live with me and I cannot keep work and his care going alone; my parents offered to help.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: A practical care arrangement with family help, without declaring the transition painless or calling help abandonment.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Matches age 22 in the proposed active episode ending May 1930.

positiveCases.input: I am working on a comparison, but the evidence is incomplete and I do not want to pretend my answer is certain.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Publishing a bounded inquiry with open questions, not a dismissed-genius vindication or a diagnosis of private doubt.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Matches the proposed age 59 at publication.

positiveCases.input: I achieved something important, but the exhausting appearances left me without expense money; they suspended me and I still need reliable work.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Recognition alongside difficult working conditions, suspension and financial uncertainty; no invented single complaint-to-suspension causal sequence.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Within the proposed 22–26 period; the synthetic reader's age does not date each historical event.

positiveCases.input: I practiced for an audition and still did not get in; I want a chance to learn, but even a trial place would be uncertain.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Unsuccessful auditions followed by seeking instruction and an uncertain trial opportunity, not accent as a measure of worth.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Within the qualified 15–19 outer envelope. Conflicting first-audition chronology remains unresolved; this does not date that audition at eighteen.

positiveCases.input: I can barely compose anymore. I want to ask for more time with unfinished work, but I cannot promise it will be ready.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Stated difficulty composing and a bounded request for time, without promising completion or inferring therapy or a cure.

positiveCases.input: I need to explain why our quiet work with children deserves funding. I can give concrete examples of what we do, but I cannot control the decision.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Explaining caring work to a decision-maker; no promise that testimony secures funding and no childhood-bullying premise.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Matches the supported age 41 in spring 1969; the exact hearing day remains unasserted.

positiveCases.input: I joined a team but mostly sit on the bench; I am considering another activity without knowing whether I will like it.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Proposed partial connection: limited playing time and an invitation to try another activity. No medical recovery, cure or guaranteed athletic success is implied.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Reader age eighteen is deliberate for adult intake and lies two years beyond the qualified 5–16 historical outer envelope. This is not an age-identical positive gold case; appropriateness and age-filter effects remain unmeasured.

positiveCases.input: I am organizing a gathering with several groups. The groups still disagree, and I keep asking myself whether anyone will come.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: Collective organization, uncertainty about turnout and unresolved disagreement; not acceptance of permanent invisibility.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Matches the proposed age 51 during the organizing episode.

positiveCases.input: I want a business of my own after years in this field. I can use my experience, but changing direction near forty still feels like a beginning.
positiveCases.comparisonBasis: An experienced move toward a self-directed business; not a claim of starting with no skills, resources or prior career.
positiveCases.ageQualification: Within the proposed 39–41 transition period; not an asserted exact shop-opening age.

negativePremiseProbes.input: My family has rejected me and I feel as though I have no worth.

disallowedPremise.claim: The first-song episode documents parental abandonment, dispossession or a recovery of personal worth.

negativePremiseProbes.input: After grief and betrayal I want to disappear for a while and take a trip that will make everything better.

disallowedPremise.claim: The difficult-book episode establishes a disappearance, a restorative train journey or travel curing grief.

negativePremiseProbes.input: I lost my job because of substance use and want a story about quitting on my own and getting my career back.

disallowedPremise.claim: The musical-learning episode documents firing, unsupervised withdrawal, abstinence or an addiction cure that restored a career.

negativePremiseProbes.input: People dismiss my ideas because they only pay attention to how I look.

disallowedPremise.claim: The paperwork episode documents rejection of an invention because of its inventor's appearance or later technological vindication.

negativePremiseProbes.input: I know my research is right, but everyone ignores it and I want to prove them wrong.

disallowedPremise.claim: The qualified comparison establishes universal dismissal of a certain conclusion, withdrawal or later vindication of that episode.

negativePremiseProbes.input: I am still upset about being bullied as a child for being different.

disallowedPremise.claim: Adult Senate testimony is a documented childhood-bullying episode, medical recovery or a reconstruction of private childhood distress.

negativePremiseProbes.input: I want an example proving that ignoring a treatment plan is how to become a great athlete.

disallowedPremise.claim: Trying a different school sport proves that medical defiance cures disability or guarantees elite athletic success.

negativePremiseProbes.input: I do the work behind a group project, but nobody lets me speak and everyone leaves me without support.

disallowedPremise.claim: The organizing episode establishes universal abandonment, never speaking publicly or accepting erasure as its lesson.
